result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers firmly choose inline tracked changes, tie it to traceability, and explain how copy-paste breaks the audit trail. B covers more of what chat is good for (open questions, drafting from scratch) and is clearer about keeping it secondary: output either never enters the document or arrives as a tracked insertion. B also adds stronger traceability details, such as logging the prompt and model version, and frames redline tedium as the main risk with a user test to check it. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick inline tracked changes, explain traceability and how copy-paste breaks the audit trail, and give similar mitigations (blocking or limiting accept-all, AI authorship attribution, small suggestions with rationales). A says more about what chat is good for (questions, drafting from scratch) and adds logging of model and prompt plus a user-testing caveat. B adds user-initiated invocation and a clearer phased plan in which chat feeds tracked suggestions. Neither is clearly stronger overall.
